title.narrative: Local Health Care for Disadvantaged Areas Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The proposed Local Health Care Sector Development Program will assist the Government of Viet Nam to implement the Master Plan for Strengthening Local Health Care Services, which sets out reforms to improve access to and the quality of the local health care (LHC) system. The design and monitoring framework is in Appendix 1. The problem tree is in Appendix 2.

Output: Service delivery models for local health care network Indicator: 12 districts in six target provinces are equipped with operational outbreak response units Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: According to the report of the Project Completion and Evaluation Firm: All 12 districts have established rapid response teams to diseases, infectious diseases and public health events according to Decision 5894/QD- MOH of MOH
Data Source: MOH project performance monitoring system and MF-MPSLHCS reported in annual project progress report

Output: Service delivery models for local health care network Indicator: 20% of CHS in six target provinces have implemented the family medicine model Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: According to the mid-term evaluation report of the independent consulting firm: In 2022, there were still no CHSs that met the criteria for operating upon the principles of family medicine (according to PAM), so the mid-term data of this indicator is evaluated as 0%. From 1 June 2024, the Pilot Implementation Support Firm sent 6 experts to 6 provinces to provide direct support to 6 PPMUs, health centers of 12 districts and 181 communes, including Son Duong, Yen Son (Tuyen Quang), Doan Hung, Yen Lap (Phu Tho), Que Son, Hiep Duc (Quang Nam), Ia Pa, K'rong Pa (Gia Lai), Dac R' Lap, Cu Jut (Dak Nong), Long Phu, Cu Lao Dung (Soc Trang) to implement the model of CHSs operating upon the principles of family medicines. By 30 June 2025, 181/181 (100%) CHSs in 12 pilot districts in 6 provinces (Dak Nong province alone has 71/71 (100%) CHSs) are operating upon the principles of family medicine. Data Source: MOH project performance monitoring system and MF-MPSLHCS reported in annual project progress report

Output: Local health care workforce development and management Indicator: 100 doctors (at least 38% women) awarded a certificate in family medicine (data disaggregated by sex and ethnicity) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: On going In 2022, CPMU organized 5 training courses for 198 health workers from Tuyen Quang, Phu Tho, Quang Nam, Soc Trang and Gia Lai provinces. Particularly, Dak Nong province did not send students to participate in this training because they already received training from the HPET Project. Out of 198 trainees, 65.6% are female, 31.3% are ethnic minorities.
The number of new trainees reached nearly 20% of the target with a budget of 50,000 USD as planned. At the time of the mid-term evaluation, the Program still did not have any funding in the plan to train 802 students to reach the end-line target.
The remaining 802 trainees are expected to be trained if ADB and MOH agree to re-allocate budget to increase fund for this activity.
Data Source: Project annual progress report

Proportion of CHS outpatient visits to total outpatient visits in last 12 months with data disaggregated by sex, age, and ethnicity Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Because the Viet Nam living standards survey is conducted every 10 years, hence, the data for 2022 must be updated from the report of the consulting firm.
According to the mid-term evaluation report of the independent consulting firm: The ratio of outpatient visits at CHSs to the total number of outpatient visits nationwide in 2022 is 22.4%, (the ratio for female is 23.5%). (Source: Statistics Division, Department of Planning - Finance, MOH).
According to the 2024 Population Living Standards Survey conducted under Decision No. 636/QD-TCTK dated 17 July 2023 of the General Statistics Office and published in May 2025: In 2024, nationwide, the ratio of people having visits to health facilities within 12 months is 23.3%, decreasing 4.4 percentage points compared to 2022. Of which, the rate of outpatient visits is 21.1% - declining by 5.3 percentage points, while the rate of inpatient visits is 4.2% - increasing by 0.6 percentage points compared to 2022.
According to the report of the Project Completion and Evaluation Firm (CCHIP), the proportion of outpatient visits at CHSs in 12 districts in 6 provinces reached 30.4%, of which 30.8% were female. The overall proportion of 6 provinces reached 26.1%, of which 26.3% were female. Data Source: Viet Nam living standards survey

At least 85% of pregnant women have four antenatal care visits during pregnancy Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: In June 2025, data collected during the field trips in the 6 targeted provinces show that only Krong Pa district (Gia Lai), Dak R'lap and Cu Jut (Dak Nong) had the rate of pregnant women having 4 or more prenatal check-ups lower than the target of 85%, but for the 12 districts as a whole, this rate was 91.3%, and the rate for ethnic minorities alone was 89.4%, all of which were higher than the target of 85%. Note that the 2024 national average of the rate of pregnant women having 4 or more prenatal check-ups was only 80% (Ministry of Health, Document of the Conference on implementing health work in 2025, Hanoi, December 2024).
Proportion of pregnant women having 4 antenatal visits during 3 trimesters at 12 Program selected districts in 2025 (updated by June 2025). According to the report of the Project Completion and Evaluation Firm, the percentage of pregnant women having 4 antenatal cares during 3 trimesters at the end of 2024 is as follows: Nationwide is 85.6%, 16 provinces participating in the Program is 87.3%; 6 selected provinces under the Grant Component is 85%; 12 districts implementing the model of CHSs operating upon the principles of family medicine is 88.5%.
All end-line targets have been achieved and exceeded (85%). However, the percentage of pregnant ethnic minority women having 4 antenatal cares during 3 trimesters is below 85%, possibly due to ethnic minorities, limited awareness, difficult life, while the women themselves and their relatives are less interested in regular prenatal check-ups.
The percentage of pregnant women having 4 antenatal cares during 3 trimesters at Program provinces: Data Source: MOH Maternal and Child Health Department data

90% of CHS meet MOH's 2014 national standards for health service delivery Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: According to the mid-term report of the consulting firm, in 2022 the average percentage of CHSs meeting the national standards nationwide reached 98.1% (Source: Statistics Division, Department of Planning - Finance, MOH).
On 9 March 2023, MOH issued Decision 1300/QD-BYT on the national criteria for CHSs by 2030, replacing Decision 4667/QD-BYT in 2014.
Data collected during the field trips in the 6 targeted provinces in June 2025: the percentage of CHSs meeting national standards for health service delivery in 6 provinces is 96,4% (Phu Tho 225/225 (100%), Tuyên Quang 133/138 (96.3%), Gia Lai 209/218 (95,8%); Soc Trang 108/108 (100%), Dak Nong 68/71 (95.8%), Quang Nam 212/233 (91%)). Data Source: MOH joint annual health review
